Obj-C filter-by-queue

Filters queue metrics CSV rows by queue-sys-id.

Usage:
  ./filter-by-queue <input.csv> <output.csv> --queue=<id>[,<id>...]
  ./filter-by-queue <input.csv> <output.csv> --queues=<id>[,<id>...]

Options:
  --help, -h    Show this help text.

Examples:
  ./filter-by-queue qmetin.csv qmetout.csv --queues=0
  ./filter-by-queue qmetin.csv qmetout.csv --queue=0,2,3

  ./filter-by-queue <input.csv> <output.csv> --queues=<id>[,<id>...]

Examples:

  ./filter-by-queue qmetin.csv qmetout.csv --queue=0,2,3

Obj-C filter-by-job

Filters event-trace log lines by job identifier.

Usage:
  ./filter-by-job <input.log> <output.log> --job=<id>[,<id>...]
  ./filter-by-job <input.log> <output.log> --jobs=<id>[,<id>...]

Options:
  --help, -h    Show this help text.

Job ids may be written with or without the leading 'j'
(for example 0 and j0 both select job j0).

Examples:
  ./filter-by-job jobin.log jobout.log --jobs=0
  ./filter-by-job jobin.log jobout.log --job=0,1,2

Options:
  --help, -h    Show this help text.

Examples:
  ./compute-use qmet.csv quse.csv

Obj-C derive-event-metrics

Derives per-job queue and service timing from an event log.

Usage:
  ./derive-event-metrics <jobin.log> <emetric.csv>

Options:
  --help, -h    Show this help text.

Output columns:
  job-id, queue-sys-id, arrival-time, time-in-queue, time-in-service,
  response-time    (arrival until first ENTERS-SERVER)
  turn-around-time (arrival until DEPART-VIA or ERROR)

A job that visits a queue more than once produces one row per visit.
Fields a visit never reached (for example a QUEUE-FULL job that never
entered a server) are left empty.

Example:
  ./derive-event-metrics job.log emetric.csv

Derives system response-time and throughput metrics from an event log.

Options:
  --help, -h    Show this help text.

Examples:
  ./derive-sys-metrics jobin.log sysmetric.csv
